description:
src/backend.rs:552-571 and 625-646 — calendars defines two typed error
enums for backend method returns:

    #[non_exhaustive]
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    pub enum AvailabilityError<E: std::error::Error + 'static> {
        #[error("principal not found")]
        NotFound,
        #[error("forbidden")]
        Forbidden,
        #[error("requested time range is too large")]
        TooLarge,
        #[error("rate limit exceeded")]
        RateLimit,
        #[error("backend error: {0}")]
        Other(#[source] E),
    }

    #[non_exhaustive]
    #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
    pub enum QueryCalendarEventsError<E: std::error::Error + 'static> {
        ExpandDurationTooLarge,
        CannotCalculateOccurrences,
        Other(#[source] E),
    }

This is a richer error vocabulary than what the canonical mail-server
uses — mail-server returns `Result<T, Self::Error>` or
`Result<T, BackendSetError<Self::Error>>` from every analogous method.
RFC 8621 has equivalent semantic shapes (Email/parse: notFound vs
notParsable; rate-limit, etc.) that are encoded ad-hoc through `Ok(bool)`
returns, `BackendSetError` variants, or backend-specific `Self::Error`
strings.

Both shapes are reasonable. The divergence question for the workspace
maintainer:

  - If calendars' typed-enum approach is correct, mail-server should be
    propagated to. Backends would gain a clearer, type-checked vocabulary
    for "expected" spec error conditions vs "unexpected" backend storage
    failures. The `thiserror` dep would propagate to mail-server.

  - If mail-server's ad-hoc approach is correct, calendars should be
    propagated FROM. AvailabilityError + QueryCalendarEventsError get
    dissolved into `Result<T, Self::Error>` returns, with internal helper
    constructors on the backend's own Error type.

Workspace AGENTS.md doesn't take a position on this. The "Error type
fragmentation" naming-conventions section mentions error-type drift as
a workspace-API concern, suggesting the question SHOULD be decided
workspace-wide.

What goes wrong for the caller depends on which way the convergence
goes:

  - Current state: a backend author writing both extensions hand-rolls
    "is this a NotFound or a storage error?" mapping in mail-server but
    gets it for free in calendars. Different mental models.
  - If calendars wins: mail-server backend authors get a one-time
    migration; future spec extensions follow calendars' shape.
  - If mail wins: calendars backend authors lose explicit dispatch on
    NotFound / TooLarge / RateLimit; future spec extensions follow
    mail's shape.

This is genuinely an opinion finding — there is no engineering basis
for one over the other unless the maintainer adopts a workspace policy.
Labeled `opinion` per /review-library-supplement convention.

Filed under api-contract,immutability because once 0.x ships with one
convention, retroactive convergence is a SemVer-breaking signature
change.

Trade-off: workspace-API consistency vs. type-safety. Either consistent
position is defensible; the current per-crate inconsistency is not.
title: Typed error enums (AvailabilityError, QueryCalendarEventsError) diverge from canonical mail-server's ad-hoc errors
